summary: I closed the one premise the newest finding still rested on — whether the staging description is the contract or stale text — and it changed the account rather than the evidence. The captured repository contains membership.md, its own membership design proposal: it defines Staging and the nonvoter to staging to voter transition, lists "AddVoter: server becomes staging unless voter" among the client operations, and in the same document declares the promotion algorithm unimplemented and left for a separate change. That splits my earlier framing: the missing promotion loop is a declared gap, not a new defect and no longer part of my claim, while the suffrage the operation installs is a direct contradiction of what the document lists — and that is the half with the measured consequence, because on a single-voter cluster the newly installed voter enters the quorum immediately and the cluster is left with no leader, applies answering not-leader and no way to remove the entry through the API. The executed comparisons and their witnesses are unchanged; what I revised is the account and the knowledge entry it rests on, with the changed premise recorded as such and the affected uses checked (none recorded yet, so the list is empty rather than invented). I also kept both readings visible as counterevidence: membership.md is phrased as a proposal and configuration.go deprecates Staging, notes the old AddStaging command was in fact AddVoter, and leaves Promote able to act only on a Staging server that nothing creates, so the maintainers may have deliberately settled on immediate voter addition with AddNonvoter as the replacement — in which case the defect is the divergence between two published descriptions and the code, not the implementation, and my scoped claim says exactly that while leaving the choice of authoritative side to the maintainers. The run now stands on three asserted findings with their receipts and limits, two refuted suspicions with their negative evidence retained, and every registered question answered.
